sections.title: Three questions, three endings
sections.content: The three place questions go together. *Hol vagy?* asks where you are (*-ban/-ben*). *Hová mész?* asks where you are going (*-ba/-be*). *Honnan jössz?* asks where you come from (*-ból/-ből*). The place word stays the same; only the ending changes. You can join 'from' and 'to' in one sentence: *Az iskolából a moziba megyek.*

sections.title: Hol? Hová? Honnan?
rows: Where are you? I am in the shop.
Where are you going? I am going to the shop.
Where do you come from? I come from the shop.
Anna comes out of the garden.

items.english: I am going from the school to the cinema.

items.spanish: Károly a kávézóban van, a kávézóból megy haza.
items.english: Károly is in the café, and goes home from the café.

sections.content: Places said with *-n/-on* (*a téren*) have a different "from" ending, *-ról/-ről*; their "to" ending comes later.
